C1.worst_defect: The hero passes the five-second test, but its first explanation leans on jargon a half-aware visitor cannot decode: "Vendure, the open-source headless commerce framework", topped by a "Pre-release · plugin 0.3.0" badge that names a plugin before the page has said what one is for.

C2.worst_defect: The home page calls the till "open-source" and the footer says "MIT licensed", yet 'Setting up the store' says self-hosting needs "your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)" without saying what RxDB Premium is or whether it costs money, so the catch is stated but not explained.
C2.where: home/desktop/02 'Before you start' > 'Setting up the store', last bullet; home/phone/05

C3.worst_defect: Step 5 of the quick start ends with a collapsed "If your store already allows vendurepos.vercel.app". It names an old domain a new user has never seen and has no context, so it reads like a leftover in the middle of the critical CORS step.

C4.worst_defect: The product's name splits halfway through the docs. Step 2 is headed "Add TallyPosPlugin", and the permission, routes, payment method and fields are all Tally (TallyPosSell, /tally/v1, tally-pos, tallySaleAt, TallyPosV51790900000000). A one-paragraph aside explains it, but a newcomer has to keep translating.

C5.worst_defect: After the two boxed cards, 'What it does today' is nine text-only items of equal weight with no visuals. The last item, "Custom items, fees and shipping", sits alone in the left column with an empty right column beside it.

C6.worst_defect: The phone hero screenshot is the till's narrow layout cut off after the first row of two products. The cart sits behind a 'Cart (3) · €20.09' tab, so the caption "A sale in progress on the live demo till" sits under a picture with no visible sale.

C7.worst_defect: Mobile Lighthouse on / still flags 53 KiB of unused JavaScript and render-blocking requests, with LCP at 2.3 s. Titles, descriptions, JSON-LD, llms.txt, sitemap, search API and the 404 are all in order.

overall_worst.defect: A first-time visitor is told the till is open source and MIT licensed. The same page then says self-hosting needs "your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)", with no word on what that is or whether it is paid. The visitor either skims past a cost they don't know about or stops trusting the 'open-source' claim.
overall_worst.where: home/desktop/02 'Setting up the store', last bullet (also connect-a-till and limitations 'Setting up the store')
overall_worst.fix: In that bullet, say in plain words that RxDB Premium is a commercial database licence from a third party and that you need it only if you build the till yourself, not if you use app.vendurepos.com, with a link to its pricing.
